messages.subject_clean: plotting AKDE on Google satellite image
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jamie,

I do this regularly. The following lines run through the process on the buffalo data. If you have any issues adapting this code to your data just let me know.

Best,
Mike

######################################################################
############        Plotting and AKDE HR on a map       #########################
######################################################################

library(ggplot2)
library(grid)
library(ctmm)
library(raster)
library(ggmap)
library(gridExtra)
library(reshape2)

data("buffalo")
cilla <- buffalo$"Cilla"

####First go through model selection and calculate the HR conditional on the best fit model

#Calculate the vg
vg.cilla <- variogram(cilla)

#Fit the variogram for the training half of the data
GUESS <- variogram.fit(vg.cilla, interactive= FALSE)

#Fit the movement models for the training half of the data
akde.mods <- ctmm.select(cilla,
                          CTMM = GUESS,
                          verbose = TRUE,
                          method = "pHREML",
                          control=list(method="pNewton",zero=TRUE))

#calculate the akde range based on the best fit model (for a more detailed UD increase the res argument)
akdeUD <- akde(cilla,akde.mods[[1]],weights=TRUE)

####Then convert the ctmm formats into formats that gpplot can handle
projection <- cilla@info$projection

iso <- SpatialPolygonsDataFrame.UD(akdeUD, proj4string=CRS(projection))
iso <- spTransform(iso,CRS("+proj=longlat"))

iso <- fortify(iso)

ud <- raster(akdeUD) # any raster you want to plot
rtp <- rasterToPolygons(ud)
rtp <- spTransform(rtp,CRS("+proj=longlat"))
rtp@data$id <- 1:nrow(rtp@data)   # add id column for join

rtpFort <- fortify(rtp, data = rtp@data)
rtpFortMer <- merge(rtpFort, rtp@data, by.x = 'id', by.y = 'id')  # join data

#Get a map centered around the data (set the zoom as appropriate)
cilla.map <- get_map(location = c(lon = median(cilla$lon), lat = median(cilla$lat)), zoom = 10,
                      maptype = "satellite", scale = 2)

# plotting the map with the HR and locations on it
ggmap(cilla.map) +
  #This controls the UD
  geom_polygon(data = rtpFortMer,
               aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group, alpha = layer),
               fill = "#046C9A", size = 1) +
  scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(1,0)) +
  #This controls the contours
  geom_path(data = iso, aes(x = long,y=lat, group = group, colour = group, lty = group)) +
  scale_color_manual(values=c("grey70","black","grey70")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("dashed","solid","dashed")) +

  #This controls the locations
  geom_point(data = cilla, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude), fill = "#FF0000", alpha = 0.8, size = 0.3, shape = 21) +

  #The rest controls the basic plot features

  #Trim axes down to the area you're interested in
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(31.75, 32.03), breaks = c(31.80,31.90,32.00)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-25.2, -24.85)) +

  #Rename the axes
  ylab(expression(paste("Latitude"))) +
  xlab(expression(paste("Longitude"))) +

  #Set
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position="none",
        axis.title.y=element_text(family = "serif", size = 12),
        axis.title.x=element_text(family = "serif", size = 12),
        axis.text.y=element_text(family = "serif"),
        axis.text.x=element_text(family = "serif")) +
  coord_flip() #Coord flip gets the plot in the same orientation as ctmm.plot

messages.subject: fitting models to ARGOS data
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dr. Fleming et al.,
I'm a MS student interested in using the ctmm package to analyze winter home ranges for a species of heron. The data was collected using the ARGOS system, and I am wondering if there is a way to incorporate the error associated with different location classes (3, 2, 1, 0) into the models. When I fit models including all location classes, the variograms do not reach an asymptote. So, I have attempted to fit the models by filtering the dataset to include only the most accurate points (location class 3, < 250 meters), but this reduces my sample sizes significantly in some cases and am still not getting good fits. I am not sure why this is. I've included plots for one individual. Thanks in advance for any insight.

> summary(fitted.mods.61)
                   dAICc DOF[mean]
OU anisotropic  0.000000  113.9902
OUF anisotropic 2.100069  114.0238
IID anisotropic 2.611538  124.0000
 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-Gd4yXUxpBt8/WmO5FjsS3LI/AAAAAAAAAXM/AqZUtk93BTUlaGQon6jRjWxVrPies_loACLcBGAs/s1600/var.65.1.png> <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-kCGyCpJGlQ0/WmO5JvwmSwI/AAAAAAAAAXQ/9xwnIaT0Ox05SPC0sr569TLRF6HHg6E4wCLcBGAs/s1600/var.65.2.png>

Kristie

messages.subject: Re: fitting models to ARGOS data
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kristie,

I'm assuming this is daily data from the variogram plots. I suppose 250 meter error would be substantial on that plot as (250 m)^2 = 6.25 hm^2.
[If the data are sampled irregularly, you can also try fast=FALSE in variogram() to reduce smoothing bias on the empirical variogram, which can look like autocorrelation.]

There is some literature on the estimated error radii of ARGOS error classes. E.g.: http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/wol1/doi/10.1111/j.1748-7692.2002.tb01025.x/abstract
For the time being you could translate those results into a GPS-like HERE data column, which is sqrt(var(x)+var(y)) IIRC, and then set error=TRUE in the model before fitting.
I'm going to be doing this in a couple of months though, to where it will import automatically. I have one last project on my plate before I will be heading a big paper on telemetry errors.

Best,
Chris
